name: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Ltd
title: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Ltd - 542760 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR1,590 crores on slow international execution, while UOV hit a record INR13,000 crores and guidance was trimmed to 10-15% growth.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR1,590 crores, lower both sequentially and year-on-year, mainly from lower execution in the international EPC segment as four overseas projects neared completion. Gross margin was about 9.9% versus 10.5% in FY26, operational EBITDA was INR78 crores (4.9% margin), and reported EBITDA of INR96 crores included forex gains; PAT rose 36% YoY to INR53 crores on lower tax. Unexecuted order value (UOV) reached a record INR13,000 crores after a Egypt West Minya award (about USD560 million), and O&M portfolio grew to 18.3 GW. Management cut its FY27 top-line growth view to 10-15% (from about 15%), pushing the revenue ramp into H2 and expecting Q2 to be similarly slow.

financial_highlights.change: Lower QoQ and YoY; management cited lower international EPC execution
+36% YoY, aided by lower effective tax rate
Scheduled term loan repayments; net debt broadly stable
vs negative INR329 crores in previous quarter
Includes 6 turnkey projects worth about INR9,000 crores yet to start execution

financial_highlights.value: More than INR3,200 crores obtained cumulatively

segments.name: International EPC
segments.commentary: Execution slowed as four projects in South Africa, Spain and Italy reached completion; three new projects (two in South Africa, one in Egypt) are expected to start executing soon. Management says the Egypt West Minya project (1,000 MWac solar plus 600 MWh BESS, JV with Hassan Allam) will add revenue from Q4 FY27 after an expected September NTP.

segments.name: Domestic EPC
segments.commentary: Domestic solar EPC market was slow for a second quarter; total orders concluded in Q1 were only INR6,400 crores versus over INR20,000 crores expected. Coal India turnkey L1 win is under DCR category with bid price locked.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Portfolio reached a record 18.3 GW; top line grew about 40% YoY. Management expects FY27 O&M revenue of INR400-450 crores versus about INR268 crores in FY26, with O&M gross margin stabilising around 20%.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Currently executing one BESS project where the BESS supply is client-furnished, so no duty or localisation exposure. Management expects BESS market ordering in value terms to roughly equal the PV market.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 10-15% (ex-Reliance), down from earlier guidance of about 15%; management expects a strong H2 with Q3 and Q4 'very, very high'.
Q2 FY27 expected to be similar to or slightly below Q1 due to delayed new order NTPs/LOAs and monsoon season.
EPC gross margin guided at 8-10%, depending on turnkey versus BoS mix; O&M gross margin around 20%.
Order book expected to be more than INR10,000 crores at FY27 end; management also indicated order book growth of 10-15%.
Overheads in absolute terms not expected to rise; as a percentage of revenue expected to decline modestly.
Negative working capital model to continue; collections from large new projects expected to improve working capital.
Term loans to be largely repaid over FY27 and FY28, after which the company expects to be almost deleveraged on fund-based lines.
capex_capacity: O&M portfolio at a record 18.3 GW, expected to contribute fully from Q3 FY27; the company added about 5.8 GW DC of commissioning last year.
Around 10.5 GW under execution this year; manpower added for project execution and about 100 GETs being trained.
Egypt West Minya project: 13-15 months execution after NTP plus a 2-month LNTP period; NTP expected September 2026.
Government of India 500 MW BESS target stated as on track; management expects 35-40 GW of market opportunity over the next 2-3 years.
Bid pipeline of 27.7 GW, about 90% India-focused, purely solar PV and BESS.
demand_pricing: Management expects INR45,000-50,000 crores of Indian orders (about 25 GW utility-scale and 35 GWh BESS) to be announced in Q3 and Q4.

Reliance Group's Kutch integrated renewable hub (5.5 lakh acres, 40+ billion units per year) is a potential large order source; timing and quantum follow Reliance's rollout. Reliance's 40 GWh battery gigafactory first phase is due for commissioning this year.
Management stated that domestic module price increases and DCR rules are not expected to hit the Coal India order, where bid prices were locked.
Management is not pursuing aggressive bids; some new entrants are bidding aggressively.
Nigeria revenue is excluded from FY27 business plans due to procedural delays.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue fall about 10% YoY, and is there a miss versus the earlier 15% growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new orders' NTP/LOA dates were delayed, so their revenue did not start in Q1, and existing UOV projects were in advanced stages with most supplies booked in prior quarters. The guidance assumed about INR200-250 crores QoQ uplift, which did not come through.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of execution bottlenecks given the heavy H2 requirement (around INR2,600-3,000 crores per quarter)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the team is geared up and manpower is being augmented for Reliance; it cited Q4 FY25 execution above INR2,500 crores as precedent. Management said it has no option but to deliver.

qa_highlights.question: How will the DCR rules and module price changes affect margins and IRRs?
qa_highlights.answer: Coal India L1 order is under DCR with prices locked. Management said the impact is seasonal at most and expects full-year EPC margins to remain at 8-10%, depending on turnkey versus BoS mix.

qa_highlights.question: Are the INR1,800 crore claims and arbitrations recoverable, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: The two large US claims are in court and may take 2-3 years. Management said LD amounts are covered by indemnity; of the Australian arbitration (about INR200 crores), about INR110 crores is covered by LD indemnity. Management said it sees no likely impact from the frivolous claims.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS sourcing strategy and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Indian battery supply chain is not mature and that Make in India tenders are largely assembly of imported components; it is evaluating partners. BESS BoS margin is similar to PV at about 10%, while battery-side margins may be lower and volatile.

qa_highlights.question: Will the order book grow 15% at FY27 end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said order book at FY27 end would be more than INR10,000 crores and that additions could be 10-15% over last year's base; Q1 FY27 UOV is already a record INR13,000 crores.

risks_watch: Execution ramp in Q3 and Q4 must reach about INR2,600-3,000 crores per quarter; any slip would weigh on the 10-15% growth guide.
Order inflow of only INR6,400 crores in Q1 versus over INR20,000 crores expected; the INR45,000-50,000 crore Q3/Q4 pipeline is management's estimate and is unconfirmed.

Large US claims in court for 2-3 years; about INR508 crores of wrongfully invoked BG claims and about INR1,054 crores of LC/BG-related receivables (around INR800 crores covered by indemnity, with INR120-130 crores expected this year).
Gross margin guidance range of 8-10% is wide; mix shift toward turnkey could lower margin percentage.
Reliance order terms, pricing and supply composition not disclosed; related-party arm's-length basis cited.
Battery supply chain localisation and DCR rules create uncertainty for BESS and domestic EPC pricing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term order book and O&M growth, but openly cautious and defensive on near-term execution, revenue timing and the reasons for the guidance cut. Management was evasive on Reliance deal economics and on the quantum of indemnity coverage for the INR3,800 crore annual-report claims.
key_quotes: We continue to remain patient and are only pursuing margin-accretive projects.
The bid pipeline continues to remain extremely robust at 27.7 gigawatt, of which almost 90% is India focused.
So we have no other option. We have to.
We remain deliberately selective, staying away from the mandates that carry land, major right-of-way or resource risk outside our control.

adds.what: O&M portfolio at record 18.3 GW, expected to contribute fully from Q3 FY27
Egypt West Minya project 1,000 MWac solar plus 600 MWh BESS (EPC, JV with Hassan Allam)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth cut to 10-15% (midpoint ~12.5%, from about 15%), with Q1 revenue of INR1,590 crores down YoY and Q2 guided similar or slightly lower; H2 ramp backed by record UOV of INR13,000 crores and O&M revenue guide of INR400-450 crores, but the INR45,000-50,000 crores of expected Indian orders are not yet concluded.
